q-7375.name: Question 1
q-7375.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side. This gives

$$
-2x+y=-10
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+y & =-10 \\ (-1)\cdot (-2x+y) & =(-1)\cdot (-10) \\ 2x-y & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is $2x-y=10.$

q-7375.html:
Question 1
?

Write y=2x−10 in standard form.

a
y=2x−10
b
2x+y−10=0
c
2x−y=10
d
y−2x=10
e
2x+y=10
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Our goal is to write the equation in the form ax+by=c, where a,b, and c are integers with no common factors and a≥0.

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side. This gives

−2x+y=−10

Now, we multiply both sides of the equation by −1:

−2x+y=−10(−1)⋅(−2x+y)=(−1)⋅(−10)2x−y=10.

Now, a,b, and c are integers with no common factors, and a≥0. So we are done!

The standard form of the line is 2x−y=10.

q-22753.name: Question 2
q-22753.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

The equation is in the form $ax+by=c.$ However, $a,b,$ and $c$ have a common factor of $2.$ So, we divide by $2$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+22y & =-8 \\ \frac{2x+22y}{2} & =\frac{-8}{2} \\ x+11y & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is $x+11y=-4.$

q-208783.name: Question 3
q-208783.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side. This gives

$$
\frac{1}{5}x+y=\frac{1}{2}
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the equation by $10:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}x+y & =\frac{1}{2} \\ 10\cdot (\frac{1}{5}x+y) & =10\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\ 2x+10y & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is 

$$
2x+10y=5.
$$
